newsitem.title: UK: UK Channel 5 dismisses BRC retuning concerns.
newsitem.headline: UK Channel 5 dismisses BRC retuning concerns.

text.p: Channel 5 Broadcasting dismissed concerns expressed on Friday by the British Retail Consortium (BRC) about plans to retune millions of video recorders nationwide before the new television channel is launched.
"We have been consulting far and wide to make sure that consumers are protected," said Sally Osman, head of public relations at Channel 5.
She said the BRC's statement was "scaremongering".
The BRC earlier issued a statement voicing concern that the retuning could invalidate product guarantees and cause "costly and unpredictable" problems.
Channel 5, which is due to begin broadcasting on January 1, 1997, must retune some 10 million video recorders nationwide to avoid interference from its signal.
It has just begun the process of sending its engineers out to households to carry out the work, which Channel 5 sees costing around 100 million stg.
Channel 5 Broadcasting is a consortium grouping British media companies United News & Media and Pearson Plc plus broadcaster CLT of Luxembourg and U.S. investment firm Warburg Pincus.
